label: Blocked account
title: Plan your funding
description: Understand the blocked account and how to access your funds.
introduction: The most critical financial requirement for obtaining a German student visa is proof of sufficient funds to cover living expenses. Currently, Nepali students need at least €11,904 per year, which translates to €992 per month, deposited in a blocked account. As of November 2025, this amount equals approximately NPR 17–18 lakhs, and the exact conversion varies with exchange rates.

sections.title: How the Blocked Account Works
sections.content:
- Open account with authorized provider (Deutsche Bank, Fintiba, Expatrio, etc.)
- Deposit full year’s amount (€11,904) before visa application
- The account gets blocked until you arrive in Germany
- After arrival, withdraw €992 monthly for living expenses
- Funds remain protected and cannot be accessed in full at once

label: Living costs
title: Build your monthly budget
description: Compare cities and plan for everyday expenses.
introduction: Understanding actual living expenses while studying in Germany helps in financial planning beyond the visa requirement. Rent is the biggest variable depending on your city choice.

sections.title: Cities with Lower Living Costs
sections.content: Leipzig, Dresden, Jena, Erfurt, Halle. Estimated budget: €750–€950 per month.

sections.title: Cities with Higher Living Costs
sections.content: Munich, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Stuttgart, Berlin. Estimated budget: €1,000–€1,400+ per month.

sections.title: Typical Monthly Breakdown
sections.content:
- Rent (Shared/Dorm): €300–€750
- Health Insurance: ~€125 (Student Public)
- Food & Groceries: €150–€250
- Transport: €0–€49 (Deutschland-Ticket)
- Internet/Phone: €30–€50

label: Visa interview
title: Prepare for your interview
description: Review practical tips, then open the questions to practise.
introduction:
As you study in Germany from Nepal, you need to attend a visa interview at the German Embassy.

- Be Honest and Clear: Answer all questions truthfully about your study plans
- Know Your Program: Understand your course structure, subjects, and career relevance
- Explain Return Plans: Demonstrate strong ties to Nepal and intention to return
- Show Financial Clarity: Explain your funding sources confidently
- Professional Appearance: Dress formally and maintain respectful demeanor
- Organize Documents: Keep all papers well-organized for easy access

sections.title: Practice common interview questions
sections.content:
- Why did you choose to study in Germany?
- Why this specific university and program?
- How will this degree help your career in Nepal?
- Who is funding your education?
- What are your plans after completing your studies?
- Do you have any relatives in Germany?

label: After graduation
title: Explore your next steps
description: Choose an option below to read its requirements and benefits.

sections.title: Job Seeker Visa
sections.content:
After completing the degree, Germany offers an 18-month job seeker visa. This allows students to stay while looking for a job related to their course.

Benefits

- Students get 18 months to find suitable job
- Can take temporary jobs during job search
- No restrictions on number of job interviews
- Transition directly to a work visa upon securing a job

Requirements

- Need to complete degree from German university
- Health insurance coverage
- Proof of financial means (blocked account or income)
- Passport validity

sections.title: EU Blue Card
sections.content:
For highly qualified professionals, the EU Blue Card offers long-term residence and work authorization throughout the European Union.

Eligibility

- Recognized university degree (German or equivalent)
- Job offer with minimum annual salary (€58,400 in 2025, lower for shortage occupations)
- Employment contract

Benefits

- Valid for up to 4 years
- Family reunification rights
- Path to permanent residence after 33 months (21 months with B1 German)
- Freedom to work throughout EU after 18 months

sections.title: Permanent Residence (Niederlassungserlaubnis)
sections.content:
After legally residing in Germany for 5 years, you can apply for permanent residence.

Requirements and Benefits

- 5 years continuous legal residence
- Secure income and accommodation
- German language proficiency (B1 level)
- Basic knowledge of German legal and social system
- Adequate retirement provisions
- No criminal record
- Unlimited residence and work rights
- Full access to social security benefits
- Family reunification
- No renewal required

sections.title: German Citizenship
sections.content:
After 8 years of legal residence (can be reduced to 6–7 years in special cases), you may apply for German citizenship.

- Nepal does not allow dual citizenship
- Must renounce Nepali citizenship to acquire German citizenship
- Requires extensive integration (German language C1 and civic knowledge)
- Offers full political rights and EU passport benefits
